candidate.title: iCLIP
candidate.scope: The individual-nucleotide resolution CLIP (iCLIP) workflow in the middle row of the supplied Illumina image, from RNA-protein complex to amplified cDNA. The assigned card is a single source row, and the verified collection page captions the same route as iCLIP. PAR-CLIP above, BrdU-CLIP below, the clipped irCLIP row at the upper edge, and the chemical/QR graphics at right are neighboring context, not branches of the assigned row. The diagram route is retained with an explicit primary-paper correction to immunoprecipitation/adaptor order. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete protocol or a claim that all later iCLIP implementations are identical. Primary-paper clarification identifies the barcoded cleavable component as the reverse-transcription oligonucleotide; adjacency to RNA in the drawing is not a separate barcode-ligation operation. The endpoint is the depicted cDNA library; sequencing/mapping interpretation is explained from the primary paper without adding unshown analysis operations.

states.label: Barcoded reverse-transcription primer with cleavable adaptor regions
features: The drawing labels Barcode and Cleavable adaptor at the RNA-to-cDNA interface.

The primary implementation includes an experiment barcode and a random molecule barcode; the latter supports discrimination of original cDNAs from PCR duplicates.
The adjacent placement of these labels beside peptide-bearing RNA does not mean that the barcode is part of the biological RNA or was added by proteinase K.

evidence.quote: Here, we exploited this apparent limitation to achieve single nucleotide resolution by capturing these truncated cDNAs through the introduction of a second adapter after reverse transcription via self-circularization (Fig. 1).

states.label: Linear amplified cDNA library
features: The cDNA circle has been opened at the adaptor interface and PCR-amplified.
The DNA library represents RNA molecules recovered through the selected protein and their reverse-transcription endpoints; the sequenced material is DNA rather than the protein or residual peptide.
In the primary implementation, reads begin with barcode followed by the sequence at the cDNA truncation endpoint, permitting crosslink-site inference.
The library reports selected crosslinked RNA contacts, not a direct count of total cellular RNA or all protein occupancy; this follows from protein-directed recovery and RT-endpoint capture.

operations.information_effect: Preserves a physical RNA-protein contact for subsequent protein-directed selection.

operations.label: Proteinase K
operations.description: Digest the protein in the selected complex, yielding RNA bearing residual crosslinked peptide rather than fully peptide-free RNA. The proteinase icon denotes the acting reagent, not a separate workflow branch.

operations.label: cDNA truncates at binding site
operations.description: Copy the adaptor-bearing, peptide-marked RNA into cDNA using the barcoded primer. Synthesis can terminate at the residual peptide, leaving a truncated cDNA with the primer-derived barcode and cleavable adaptor regions. The drawing labels the output rather than naming RT; the primary caption identifies this transformation.
operations.mechanism: Peptide-induced premature termination of reverse transcription.
operations.information_effect: The RNA sequence identifies the contacted transcript/region, while the cDNA endpoint reports a crosslink-associated position. The barcode tracks original cDNA identity through amplification; it does not encode the protein identity.

operations.label: Circularize
operations.description: Join the ends of the recovered cDNA to form a circle, retaining its truncation boundary and the primer-derived adaptor segments. The RNA/peptide template drawn at the preceding stage is not carried into the DNA circle.
operations.mechanism: Self-circularization of single-stranded cDNA, placing the pre-existing adaptor regions into an arrangement that supports amplification after linearization.
operations.information_effect: Circularization captures truncated cDNAs for the downstream amplification interface rather than requiring RT to traverse the peptide site.
